seo_title: Grade 6 Fractions, Decimals and Percents Worksheets (Ontario Math): Free with Answer Key
standard_text: Read, represent, compare, and order fractions, decimals up to thousandths, and whole-number percents, and describe the equivalences among them
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 fractions, decimals and percents worksheets for the Ontario curriculum: equivalent fractions and simplest form, mixed numbers, 3/8 = 0.375, decimals to percents, ordering mixed forms and word problems. 100 math questions with an answer key for EQAO practice.
key_big: A fraction is a division: 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. Percent means out of 100: 0.4 = 40%.
key_sub: Know the key facts: 1/2 = 0.5 = 50%, 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%, 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%, 1/5 = 0.2 = 20%. To compare, change everything into decimals with the same number of places.
body_html:
Equivalent fractions

Equivalent fractions name the same amount. Multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number. A fraction is in simplest form when the only common factor of the top and bottom is 1.

Example

Write 912 in simplest form.

3 is a factor of 9 and 12. 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

Answer: 34

Improper fraction to mixed number

Write 114 as a mixed number.

11 ÷ 4 = 2 R 3. That is 2 wholes and 3 quarters.

Answer: 2 34

Fractions and decimals

A fraction is a division: 38 means 3 ÷ 8. Divide the numerator by the denominator. If the denominator goes into 10, 100 or 1000, you can make an equivalent fraction instead.

Quicker way

Write 720 as a decimal.

20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 720 = 35100.

Answer: 0.35

Decimals and percents

Percent means out of 100. To change a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100: 0.4 = 40%. To change a percent to a decimal, divide by 100: 7% = 0.07.

Comparing and ordering

Change everything into the same form first. Decimals with the same number of places are easiest to compare.

Example

Order 0.35, 38 and 37% from least to greatest.

0.35 = 0.350. 38 = 0.375. 37% = 0.370. Compare 350, 370 and 375 thousandths.

Answer: 0.35, 37%, 38

Who did better?

Maya scored 21 out of 25. Owen scored 17 out of 20.

2125 = 84100 = 84%. 1720 = 85100 = 85%.

Answer: Owen, with the higher percent

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about fractions, decimals and percents in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Grade 6 math curriculum, students read, represent, compare and order fractions, decimals to thousandths and whole-number percents, and explain how they are equivalent, for example 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%.

faq.q: How do you change a fraction to a decimal?
faq.a: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. If the denominator goes into 10, 100 or 1000, make an equivalent fraction instead: 7/20 = 35/100 = 0.35.

faq.q: How do you compare fractions, decimals and percents?
faq.a: Change them all into decimals with the same number of decimal places, then compare. For 0.35, 3/8 and 37%: 0.350, 0.375 and 0.370, so the order is 0.35, 37%, 3/8.

faq.q: Are fractions, decimals and percents on the Grade 6 EQAO math assessment?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 6 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, and Number, including fractions, decimals and percents, is one of the strands it covers.

sets.title: Equivalent fractions, simplest form and mixed numbers

items.q: The two bars are the same size. Which fraction is equal to 34?
items.e: Each quarter is cut into 2 equal parts, so 3 quarters become 6 eighths: 34 = 68. 56 adds 2 to the top and bottom, which does not keep the same amount.

items.q: Find the missing number: 12 = ?10
items.e: 2 × 5 = 10, so multiply the numerator by 5 too: 1 × 5 = 5. 12 = 510. 9 adds 8 to the top as well as the bottom, which does not keep the fraction the same.

items.q: Find the missing number: 23 = ?12
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. The bars show 8 of 12 parts shaded. 4 is only 12 ÷ 3; the top has to be multiplied as well.

items.q: How many twelfths are in 13?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, so 13 = 412. There are 4 twelfths. 36 comes from 12 × 3.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 56?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom by 2: 56 = 1012. 512 only changes the denominator, and 67 adds 1 to each.

items.q: Which fraction is not equal to 12?
items.e: In 36, 510 and 612 the numerator is half of the denominator, so they equal 12. Half of 6 is 3, not 4, so 46 is not equal to 12. (It equals 23.)

items.q: Write 68 in simplest form.
items.e: Divide the top and bottom by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So 68 = 34. 38 divides only the top. 46 subtracts 2 from each.

items.q: Write 912 in simplest form.
items.e: 3 is a factor of 9 and 12. 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so 912 = 34. 312 divides only the top, and 69 takes 3 from each.

items.q: Write 1012 in simplest form.
items.e: Divide the top and bottom by 2: 1012 = 56. 5 and 6 have no common factor except 1, so it is in simplest form.

items.q: Write 812 in simplest form.
items.e: The greatest common factor of 8 and 12 is 4. 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so 812 = 23. 46 is equal, but not in simplest form: 4 and 6 can still both be divided by 2.

items.q: Which fraction is in simplest form?
items.e: 7 and 12 have no common factor except 1, so 712 is in simplest form. 410 = 25, 69 = 23 and 312 = 14.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded, in simplest form?
items.e: 9 of 12 parts are shaded: 912. The thick lines make 4 groups of 3, and 3 groups are shaded: 912 = 34. 912 is equal, but not in simplest form.

items.q: Find the missing number: 410 = 6?
items.e: Simplify first: 410 = 25. Then 2 × 3 = 6, so 5 × 3 = 15. 615 = 410. 12 adds 2 to the top and bottom, which does not keep the same amount.

items.q: Write 114 as a mixed number.
items.e: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 R 3. That is 2 wholes and 3 quarters left over: 2 34. 1 14 reads 11 as 1 and 1.

items.q: Write 176 as a mixed number.
items.e: 17 ÷ 6 = 2 R 5. That is 2 wholes and 5 sixths: 2 56. 2 65 writes the remainder and the divisor the wrong way round.

items.q: Which improper fraction is equal to 2 12?
items.e: 2 wholes = 42. Add the half: 4 + 1 = 5, so 2 12 = 52. 42 forgets to add the 1 half.

items.q: Write 3 25 as an improper fraction.
items.e: 3 wholes = 155. Add the 2 fifths: 15 + 2 = 17, so 3 25 = 175. 65 multiplies 3 × 2; the whole number is multiplied by the denominator.

items.q: Write 2 38 as an improper fraction.
items.e: 2 × 8 = 16 eighths in 2 wholes. 16 + 3 = 19, so 2 38 = 198. 58 just adds 2 + 3, and 238 writes the digits together.

items.q: Each whole is split into quarters. Which fraction is at the arrow?
items.e: Count the quarters from 0: 4 to reach 1, 8 to reach 2, then 1 more. That is 94 = 2 14. 912 uses all 12 quarters on the line as the denominator, but each whole has 4 parts.

items.q: Write 1812 as a mixed number in simplest form.
items.e: 18 ÷ 12 = 1 R 6, so 1812 = 1 612. Then simplify 612 = 12: 1 12. 1 612 and 64 are equal but not in simplest form.

items.q: Write 710 as a decimal.
items.e: 7 tenths: the 7 goes in the tenths place, the first place after the decimal point. 710 = 0.7.

items.q: Write 23100 as a decimal.
items.e: 23 hundredths: the last digit goes in the hundredths place, the second place after the point. 23100 = 0.23.

items.q: Write 9100 as a decimal.
items.e: 9 hundredths: write a 0 in the tenths place to hold it. 9100 = 0.09. 0.9 would be 9 tenths.

items.q: Write 471000 as a decimal.
items.e: 47 thousandths: the last digit goes in the thousandths place, the third place after the point. 471000 = 0.047. 0.47 would be 47 hundredths.

items.q: Write 12 as a decimal.
items.e: 12 = 510 = 0.5. 0.12 and 1.2 just write the digits of the fraction.

items.q: Write 14 as a decimal.
items.e: 14 = 25100 (multiply the top and bottom by 25) = 0.25. 0.4 uses the denominator as tenths.

items.q: Write 35 as a decimal.
items.e: 35 = 610 (multiply the top and bottom by 2) = 0.6. 0.35 just writes the digits 3 and 5.

items.q: Write 25 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 = 410 = 0.4. 2.5 is 5 ÷ 2, the wrong way round, and 0.2 is only 15.

items.q: Write 0.6 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.6 = 6 tenths = 610. Divide the top and bottom by 2: 35. 6100 would be 0.06.

items.q: Write 0.25 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.25 = 25 hundredths = 25100. Divide the top and bottom by 25: 14. 2510 would be 2.5.

items.q: Write 18 as a decimal.
items.e: 1 ÷ 8: write 1 as 1.000. 10 ÷ 8 = 1 R 2, 20 ÷ 8 = 2 R 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 18 = 0.125. 0.12 stops before the remainder is 0.

items.q: The division shows 3 ÷ 8. What is 38 as a decimal?
items.e: 30 ÷ 8 = 3 R 6, 60 ÷ 8 = 7 R 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 0.38 and 3.8 just use the digits of the fraction.

items.q: The division shows 5 ÷ 8. What is 58 as a decimal?
Write 720 as a decimal.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 720 = 35100 = 0.35. 0.7 would be 710.

items.q: Write 1125 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 1125 = 44100 = 0.44. 0.11 forgets to multiply the top by 4, and 0.36 adds 11 + 25.

items.q: Write 912 as a decimal.
items.e: Simplify first: 912 = 34. Then 34 = 75100 = 0.75.

items.q: Write 0.08 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.08 = 8 hundredths = 8100. Divide the top and bottom by 4: 225. 810 would be 0.8.

items.q: Write 0.375 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.375 has three decimal places, so it is 3751000. Divide the top and bottom by 125: 38. 375100 would be 3.75.

items.q: Write 114 as a decimal.
items.e: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 R 3, so 114 = 2 34. 34 = 0.75, so the answer is 2.75. 2.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.

items.q: Write 2 38 as a decimal.
items.e: The 2 wholes stay the same. 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. So 2 38 = 2.375.

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 20 of the 100 squares are shaded. Percent means out of 100, so it is 20%. 80% is the white part.

items.q: Which shows the shaded part as a decimal and a percent?
items.e: 35 of 100 squares: 35100 = 0.35 = 35%. 0.65 and 65% describe the white part.

items.q: What decimal of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 7 of 100 squares = 7 hundredths = 0.07 = 7%. 0.7 would be 70 squares.

items.q: Write 0.4 as a percent.
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 40 hundredths = 40%. Multiply by 100: 0.4 × 100 = 40. 4% would be 0.04.

items.q: Write 0.07 as a percent.
items.e: 0.07 = 7 hundredths = 7%. 70% would be 0.7.

items.q: Write 0.25 as a percent.
items.e: 0.25 = 25 hundredths = 25%. Multiply by 100: the digits move 2 places to the left.

items.q: Write 0.9 as a percent.
items.e: 0.9 = 0.90 = 90 hundredths = 90%. 9% would be 0.09.

items.q: Write 0.8 as a percent.
Write 0.12 as a percent.
items.e: 0.12 = 12 hundredths = 12%. 120% would be 1.2.

items.q: Write 45% as a decimal.
items.e: 45% = 45 hundredths = 0.45. Divide by 100: the digits move 2 places to the right.

items.q: Write 8% as a decimal.
items.e: 8% = 8 hundredths. Hundredths are the second place after the point: 0.08. 0.8 is 80%.

items.q: Write 60% as a decimal.
items.e: 60% = 60 hundredths = 6 tenths = 0.6. 0.06 is only 6%.

items.q: Write 100% as a decimal.
items.e: 100% means 100 out of 100, the whole amount: 100 ÷ 100 = 1.

items.q: Write 3% as a decimal.
items.e: 3% = 3 hundredths = 0.03. 0.3 would be 30%.

items.q: Write 14 as a percent.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 25%. 14% just writes the digits, and 4% and 40% use only the denominator.

items.q: Write 35 as a percent.
items.e: 35 = 60100 = 60%. 35% just writes the digits 3 and 5.

items.q: Write 320 as a percent.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 320 = 15100 = 15%. 60% comes from 3 × 20.

items.q: Write 925 as a percent.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 925 = 36100 = 36%. 34% adds 9 + 25.

items.q: Write 5% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 5% = 5100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 120. 15 is 20%, not 5%.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 = 0.50 = 12 = 50%. 5% is 0.05, only one tenth as much.

sets.title: Compare and order fractions, decimals and percents

items.q: Compare 0.7 and 0.65.
items.e: 0.7 = 0.70. Compare the tenths: 7 tenths > 6 tenths. So 0.7 > 0.65, even though 65 > 7.

items.q: Compare 0.09 and 0.1.
items.e: 0.1 = 0.10. Compare the tenths: 0 < 1. So 0.09 < 0.1.

items.q: Compare 0.35 and 0.305.
items.e: Write both with 3 decimal places: 0.350 and 0.305. Compare the hundredths: 5 > 0. So 0.35 > 0.305. More digits does not mean a greater number.

items.q: Compare 18 and 16.
c: 18 = 16
18 > 16
18 < 16
items.e: Both have 1 part. Eighths are smaller parts than sixths, because the whole is cut into more pieces. So 18 < 16. A bigger denominator does not make a bigger fraction.

items.q: Compare 512 and 58.
c: 512 > 58
512 < 58
512 = 58
items.e: Same numerator: 5 twelfths and 5 eighths. Twelfths are smaller parts than eighths, so 512 < 58.

items.q: Compare 0.6 and 35.
items.e: 35 = 610 = 0.6. So 0.6 = 35.

items.q: Compare 40% and 0.04.
Compare 15 and 15%.
items.e: 15 = 20100 = 20%. 20% > 15%, so 15 > 15%.

items.q: Compare 38 and 0.35.
items.e: Change the fraction to a decimal: 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 0.375 > 0.350, so 38 > 0.35.

items.q: Compare 23 and 0.66.
items.e: 23 = 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666…, which is a little more than 0.66 = 0.660. So 23 > 0.66.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
0.5, 0.45, 0.405, 0.054
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405, 0.054. Compare 500, 450, 405 and 54 thousandths. So 0.054, 0.405, 0.45, 0.5.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: As decimals: 0.450, 25 = 0.400, 42% = 0.420, 0.405. The greatest is 0.45.

items.q: Which is the least?
items.e: As decimals: 0.205, 14 = 0.250, 0.300, 22% = 0.220. The least is 0.205, even though it has the most digits.

items.q: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal parts. What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: 8 equal parts, so each part is 18. The dot is 3 parts along: 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 0.3 would be 3 tenths, but the line has 8 parts, not 10.

items.q: The line from 0% to 100% is split into 5 equal parts. What percent is at the red dot?
items.e: 5 equal parts, so each part is 15 = 20%. The dot is 4 parts along: 4 × 20% = 80%. 40% counts each part as 10%.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
0.35, 38, 37%
items.e: Make them all decimals with 3 places: 0.350, 38 = 0.375, 37% = 0.370. So the order is 0.35, 37%, 38.

items.q:
Order from greatest to least:
0.8, 34, 79%
items.e: As decimals: 0.8 = 0.80, 34 = 0.75, 79% = 0.79. Greatest first: 0.8, 79%, 34.

items.q: Which number is between 0.3 and 0.4?
items.e: 38 = 0.375, which is between 0.3 and 0.4. 14 = 0.25 and 45% = 0.45 are not, and 0.43 is more than 0.4.

items.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
items.e: 0.6 = 0.600, 23 = 0.666… and 70% = 0.700. So 0.6, 23, 70%.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
1.2, 1 14, 1.15
items.e: As decimals: 1.2 = 1.20, 1 14 = 1.25, 1.15. So 1.15, 1.2, 1 14. 1.15 has more digits but is the least.

sets.title: Word problems: test scores, chances and sales

items.q: Owen scores 18 out of 20 on a spelling test. What percent does he score?
items.e: 1820 = 90100 (multiply the top and bottom by 5) = 90%. 10% is the part he got wrong.

items.q: The forecast says there is a 75% chance of snow tomorrow. What fraction is that?
items.e: 75% = 75100. Divide the top and bottom by 25: 34. 14 is the chance that it does not snow.

items.q: There is a 75% chance of snow tomorrow. What is the chance that it does not snow, as a decimal?
items.e: Snow or no snow makes 100%. 100% − 75% = 25% = 0.25. 0.75 is the chance of snow.

items.q: In a Grade 6 class, 35 of the students walk to school. What percent of the class walk?
items.e: 35 = 60100 = 60%. 35% just writes the digits 3 and 5.

items.q: At one school, 0.7 of the students stay for lunch. The rest go home for lunch. What percent go home?
items.e: 0.7 = 70% stay. All the students are 100%, so 100% − 70% = 30% go home.

items.q: A hockey team won 12 of its 16 games this season. What percent of its games did it win?
items.e: 1216 = 34 (divide by 4) = 75100 = 75%. 25% is the games it did not win.

items.q: Store A has 14 off a pair of skates. Store B has 20% off the same skates. Which store takes off more?
items.e: 14 = 25%, and 25% > 20%. The skates cost the same to start with, so Store A takes off more.

items.q: On a math test, Mateo scores 21 out of 25 and Aiden scores 17 out of 20. Who has the higher percent?
items.e: 2125 = 84100 = 84%. 1720 = 85100 = 85%. 85% > 84%, so Aiden does better, even with fewer marks.

items.q: Zoe’s tablet battery shows 45%. What fraction of a full charge is that?
items.e: 45% = 45100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 920. 451000 would be 0.045.

items.q: Sofia cuts a 3 m rope into 4 equal pieces for a canoe trip. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3 ÷ 4 = 34 m = 0.75 m. 1.33 m is about 4 ÷ 3, the wrong way round. 0.25 m would come from a 1 m rope.

items.q: 5 pizzas are shared equally among 8 students at a class party. How much pizza does each student get, as a decimal?
items.e: 5 ÷ 8 = 58. 50 ÷ 8 = 6 R 2, 20 ÷ 8 = 2 R 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5, so each student gets 0.625 of a pizza. 1.6 is 8 ÷ 5.

items.q: Two maple syrup jugs are the same size. Jug A is 38 full. Jug B is 0.4 full. Which jug has more syrup?
items.e: 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 0.4 = 0.400. 0.400 > 0.375, so Jug B has more.

items.q: There are 50 students in Grade 6. 23 of them bike to school. What percent bike?
items.e: 2350 = 46100 (multiply the top and bottom by 2) = 46%. 27% uses the 27 students who do not bike.

items.q: $2 is shared equally among 5 friends. How much does each friend get?
items.e: $2 ÷ 5 = 25 of a dollar = 410 = $0.40 = 40¢. $2.50 is 5 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: Nathan scores 33 out of 40 on a reading test. Maya scores 82%. Who has the higher score?
items.e: 3340 = 33 ÷ 40 = 0.825. 82% = 0.820. 0.825 > 0.820, so Nathan has the higher score.

items.q: Four stores have a sale on the same winter boots. Which sign gives the biggest discount?
items.e: As decimals: 0.35, 13 = 0.333…, 0.30 and 14 = 0.25. 0.35 is the greatest, so 35% off.

items.q: Chloe has paddled 0.375 of the way across a lake in a canoe. What fraction of the way is that?
items.e: 0.375 = 3751000. Divide the top and bottom by 125: 38. 375100 would be 3.75.

items.q: In gym class, Noah scores on 7 of 8 shots on net. Liam scores on 85% of his shots. Who has the higher scoring rate?
items.e: 78 = 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875. 85% = 0.850. 0.875 > 0.850, so Noah has the higher rate.

items.q: Mei’s water bottle holds 1 L. She drinks 0.35 L at recess. What fraction of the bottle is left?
items.e: 1 − 0.35 = 0.65 L is left. 0.65 = 65100 = 1320 (divide by 5). 720 is the part she drank.

items.q: A quiz has 20 questions. Hana gets 0.85 of them right. How many questions does she get right?
items.e: 0.85 = 85100 = 1720. 1720 of 20 questions is 17 questions. 3 is the number she gets wrong.
